questions.question: A ball rolls off a table with a horizontal velocity of 1.2 m s^-1. It takes 0.9 s to reach the ground and lands a horizontal distance s from the table. Which expression gives s in metres? A: 1.2^2 / (2 x 9.81); B: 1.2 x 0.9; C: 0.5 x 9.81 x 0.9^2; D: (1.2 x 0.9) + (0.5 x 9.81 x 0.9^2).
steps: Horizontal and vertical motions are independent.
No horizontal force acts (air resistance ignored), so the horizontal velocity stays 1.2 m s^-1.
Horizontal distance = horizontal velocity x time: s = 1.2 x 0.9 = 1.08 m.
C gives the vertical drop, not s; A and D mix vertical and horizontal motion wrongly, so the answer is B.

questions.question: A sphere falls from rest and a camera records its position at constant time intervals. Image 1 is at the release point and Image 2 is one spacing below it. Positions P, Q, R and S follow below Image 2, each one more spacing lower (P is 2 spacings below Image 1, Q is 3, R is 4, S is 5). Where is the sphere in Image 3? A: P; B: Q; C: R; D: S.
questions.answer: C - R (4 spacings below the release point)
steps: From rest, s = 0.5 g t^2, so distance fallen is proportional to t^2.
Image 2 is taken at time T and Image 3 at time 2T.
Distance at 2T = (2T/T)^2 = 4 times the distance at T.
Image 2 is 1 spacing below the release point, so Image 3 is 4 spacings below it.
On the diagram, 4 spacings below Image 1 is position R, so the answer is C.

questions.question: A ball bearing is released from rest at position A and the time t to fall a distance l is measured by a timer. This is repeated for decreasing values of l. Explain how the measurements can be used to find g in m s^-2, including a sketch of the graph the student would expect.
questions.answer: Plot l against t^2: a straight line through the origin with gradient g/2, so g = 2 x gradient.
steps: The ball starts from rest, so u = 0 and s = ut + 0.5at^2 becomes l = 0.5 g t^2.
Compare with y = mx: plotting l (y-axis) against t^2 (x-axis) gives a straight line through the origin.
Calculate t^2 for each measured t (repeat timings and average first).
Sketch: a straight line through the origin with positive gradient, l on the y-axis and t^2 on the x-axis.
Draw the line of best fit and find its gradient = g/2.
g = 2 x gradient, in m s^-2 when l is in m and t in s.

questions.question: Two photographs, taken 83 ms apart, show a popcorn kernel just before popping and the popped kernel at its maximum height. A scale bar beside the photographs represents 1 cm. Use the photographs to determine the maximum height reached after popping.
questions.answer: Maximum height about 3.5 cm = 0.035 m (measured centre to centre with the 1 cm scale)
steps: Measure the vertical distance between the same point (the centre) of the kernel in each photograph.
Measure the length of the 1 cm scale bar on the same page.
On the page the rise is about 3.5 times the scale bar length.
Maximum height = 3.5 x 1 cm = 3.5 cm = 0.035 m.
Check: rising for 83 ms to the top, h = 0.5 x 9.81 x 0.083^2 = 0.034 m, which agrees.

questions.question: Using the maximum height found from the photographs (about 0.035 m), calculate the initial speed of the popped popcorn kernel.
steps: At maximum height v = 0; take upwards as positive so a = -9.81 m s^-2 and s = 0.035 m.
Check with the 83 ms: u = g t = 9.81 x 0.083 = 0.81 m s^-1, about the same.

questions.question: Water makes up 14% of the 0.11 g mass of an unpopped kernel. When it pops, the water is ejected downwards as steam and the rest of the kernel moves upwards at 1.5 m s^-1. The kernel is at rest before popping. Calculate the speed at which the steam is ejected.
steps: Mass of steam = 0.14 x 0.11 g = 0.0154 g.
Mass of popped kernel = 0.11 - 0.0154 = 0.0946 g.
Momentum before = 0, so momentum of kernel upwards = momentum of steam downwards.
0.0946 x 1.5 = 0.0154 x v (units of mass cancel, so grams can be used).

questions.question: Which of these units could only be used for a scalar quantity? A: m s^-1; B: m s^-2; C: kg m s^-2; D: kg m^-3.
steps: m s^-1 can be speed (scalar) or velocity (vector), so A is not only scalar.
m s^-2 is the unit of acceleration, a vector.
kg m s^-2 is the newton, the unit of force, a vector.
kg m^-3 is the unit of density, which has no direction, so only a scalar: D.

questions.question: A ball bearing falls vertically from rest through 50 cm in 0.32 s. Which expression gives its acceleration in m s^-2? A: 1 / 0.32^2; B: 0.5 / 0.32; C: 100 / 0.32^2; D: 50 / 0.32.
steps: Convert the distance to SI units: s = 50 cm = 0.50 m.
From rest, s = 0.5 a t^2, so a = 2s / t^2.
a = 9.8 m s^-2, so the answer is A (C forgets to convert cm to m).

questions.question: A trolley starts from rest at A and runs down a straight track to B. A is 0.50 m higher than B and 2.0 m from B horizontally. Air resistance and friction are negligible. Show that the trolley reaches B with a speed of about 3 m s^-1.
questions.answer: v = 3.1 m s^-1 at B (about 3 m s^-1)
steps: Length of slope AB = sqrt(2.0^2 + 0.50^2) = 2.06 m.
sin(theta) = 0.50 / 2.06 = 0.243, so the acceleration down the slope a = g sin(theta) = 9.81 x 0.243 = 2.38 m s^-2.
v = sqrt(9.81) = 3.13 m s^-1, which is about 3 m s^-1.
Check by energy: v = sqrt(2 g h) = sqrt(2 x 9.81 x 0.50) = 3.13 m s^-1.

questions.question: After reaching B (0.50 m below A, 2.0 m horizontally from A, starting from rest) the trolley continues along a horizontal track 1.0 m long to C. Friction is negligible. Determine the time taken to move from A to C.
questions.answer: Time from A to C about 1.6 s (1.64 s)
steps: A to B: slope length 2.06 m, speed at B = 3.13 m s^-1 from rest.
Average speed on the slope = (0 + 3.13) / 2 = 1.57 m s^-1, so t1 = 2.06 / 1.57 = 1.32 s.
B to C: no friction, so speed stays 3.13 m s^-1 on the horizontal track.
Total time = 1.32 + 0.32 = 1.64 s, about 1.6 s.

questions.question: A stone is projected horizontally at 3.8 m s^-1 from the top of a cliff 12 m above the ground. Calculate the horizontal distance from the bottom of the cliff to where the stone hits the ground.
steps: Vertically: u = 0, s = 12 m, a = 9.81 m s^-2.
Horizontally the velocity is constant at 3.8 m s^-1.
Horizontal distance = 3.8 x 1.56 = 5.9 m.

questions.question: A rock falls from rest through a small distance s onto Mars, hitting it at velocity vM. Another rock falls from rest through the same distance s onto Earth, hitting it at velocity vE. Gravitational acceleration on Mars is 0.38g. Calculate the ratio vM / vE.
steps: From rest, v^2 = u^2 + 2as gives v^2 = 2as, so v = sqrt(2as).
Mars: vM = sqrt(2 x 0.38g x s). Earth: vE = sqrt(2 x g x s).
vM / vE = sqrt(0.38g x s / (g x s)) = sqrt(0.38).

questions.question: A ball moving horizontally at 7.0 m s^-1 hits a vertical wall and rebounds along its path at 5.0 m s^-1. Its acceleration while touching the wall is 300 m s^-2. Which expression gives the contact time t? A: t = (-5 - 7) / (-300); B: t = (5 - 7) / (-300); C: t = (-5 - 7) / 300; D: t = (5 - 7) / 300.
steps: Take the initial direction (towards the wall) as positive: u = +7 m s^-1.
The ball rebounds, so v = -5 m s^-1.
The acceleration acts away from the wall, so a = -300 m s^-2.
The answer is A; the other options give a negative time or ignore the change of direction.

questions.question: A car travelling at 3 m s^-1 accelerates uniformly in a straight line for 15 m, reaching 5 m s^-1. Which expression gives its acceleration in m s^-2? A: (5 - 3) / 15; B: (5 - 3) / (2 x 15); C: (5^2 - 3^2) / 15; D: (5^2 - 3^2) / (2 x 15).
steps: Known: u = 3 m s^-1, v = 5 m s^-1, s = 15 m; time is not given.
Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as, which has no t.
a = 16 / 30 = 0.53 m s^-2, so the answer is D.

questions.question: A racing car passes point P at 35 m s^-1, accelerates uniformly and passes point Q 5.0 s later at 50 m s^-1. Which expression gives the distance s in metres between P and Q? A: (50^2 - 35^2) / (2 x 5); B: (35 x 5) + (0.5 x 9.81 x 5^2); C: 0.5 x (35 + 50) x 5; D: 35 + (9.81 x 5).
steps: For uniform acceleration, s = 0.5 (u + v) t.
B and D wrongly use g (the car is not falling); A divides by 2 x 5 (time) instead of 2a, so the answer is C.

questions.question: A car moving at 25 m s^-1 towards a stop sign brakes 20 m before the sign and decelerates uniformly to rest just before it. Which gives the magnitude of the deceleration in m s^-2? A: 25 / 40; B: 25 / 20; C: 25^2 / 40; D: 25^2 / 20.
steps: Known: u = 25 m s^-1, v = 0, s = 20 m.
Magnitude of deceleration = 25^2 / (2 x 20) = 25^2 / 40.
= 625 / 40 = 15.6 m s^-2, so the answer is C.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards. Which row gives the magnitude of its initial acceleration and of its acceleration at maximum height? A: 0 and 9.81 m s^-2; B: 9.81 m s^-2 and 0; C: 9.81 m s^-2 and 9.81 m s^-2; D: 0 and 0.
questions.answer: C - 9.81 m s^-2 at launch and 9.81 m s^-2 at maximum height
steps: Once released, the only force on the ball is its weight (air resistance ignored).
So the acceleration is g = 9.81 m s^-2 downwards throughout the flight.
At maximum height the velocity is zero but the acceleration is still 9.81 m s^-2.
Both values are 9.81 m s^-2, so the answer is C.

questions.question: An object on the Moon falls 0.32 m from rest in 0.63 s. Which expression gives the acceleration due to gravity on the Moon in m s^-2? A: 0.32 / (2 x 0.63); B: 0.32 / (2 x 0.63^2); C: (2 x 0.32) / 0.63^2; D: (2 x 0.32) / 0.63.
steps: From rest, u = 0, so s = 0.5 g t^2.
Rearrange: g = 2s / t^2.
g = 1.6 m s^-2, so the answer is C.

questions.question: A tennis ball machine projects balls horizontally from a height of 2.54 m. Show that the time taken for a ball to reach the ground is about 0.7 s.
steps: Projected horizontally, so the initial vertical velocity u = 0.
Vertically s = 2.54 m and a = 9.81 m s^-2, so s = 0.5 g t^2.
t = 0.72 s, which is about 0.7 s.

questions.question: The ball, projected horizontally from 2.54 m and taking 0.72 s to land, lands 17.89 m horizontally from the machine. Calculate the velocity of the ball as it is projected.
steps: There is no horizontal force, so the horizontal velocity is constant.
The time in the air is the fall time from 2.54 m: t = sqrt(2 x 2.54 / 9.81) = 0.72 s.
v = horizontal distance / time = 17.89 / 0.72.
v = 24.9 m s^-1, about 25 m s^-1, directed horizontally.

questions.question: The horizontal launch velocity of the tennis ball (from 2.54 m) is increased. Explain how this affects the angle at which the ball hits the ground.
questions.answer: The ball hits the ground at a smaller angle to the horizontal (a shallower angle).
steps: The height and the vertical acceleration are unchanged, so the time of fall stays about 0.72 s.
So the vertical velocity at impact is unchanged: sqrt(2 x 9.81 x 2.54) = 7.1 m s^-1.
The horizontal velocity is larger, and it stays constant during the flight.
Angle below horizontal: tan(theta) = vertical velocity / horizontal velocity.
A larger horizontal velocity gives a smaller tan(theta), so a smaller angle to the ground.

questions.question: A firework is designed to explode at its maximum height of 350 m. Show that the vertical component of its velocity at launch is about 80 m s^-1.
questions.answer: Vertical launch velocity = 83 m s^-1, about 80 m s^-1
steps: At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero: v = 0.
Take upwards positive: s = 350 m, a = -9.81 m s^-2.

questions.question: The vertical launch component (83 m s^-1, needed to reach 350 m) depends on the initial velocity v and the angle theta between v and the horizontal. Sketch a graph of the initial velocity needed to reach 350 m against theta, for theta from 0 to 90 degrees.
questions.answer: A curve falling from very large values near theta = 0 to a minimum of about 83 m s^-1 at 90 degrees, flattening out there (v = 83 / sin(theta)).
steps: The vertical component must be 83 m s^-1, so v sin(theta) = 83 and v = 83 / sin(theta).
As theta tends to 0, sin(theta) tends to 0 so v becomes very large: the curve never touches the v-axis.
Sample values: theta = 30 gives 166 m s^-1, 45 gives 117 m s^-1, 60 gives 96 m s^-1.
At theta = 90, sin(theta) = 1 so v = 83 m s^-1 (labelled on the axis), the minimum value.
The curve is always decreasing and its gradient becomes zero at 90 degrees.

questions.question: A student estimates the time between seeing and hearing the firework explode, and the angle phi subtended at the eye from the top to the bottom of the exploded firework. Describe how the student could use these to find the maximum diameter of the firework.
questions.answer: Distance = speed of sound x time delay; diameter = distance x phi (phi in radians), or 2 x distance x tan(phi/2).
steps: Light arrives almost instantly, so the delay is the time for the sound to travel to the student.
Distance to the firework = speed of sound (about 340 m s^-1) x time delay.
The diameter subtends angle phi at the student's eye.
Diameter = distance x phi with phi in radians (small angle), or diameter = 2 x distance x tan(phi / 2).

questions.question: A basketball is thrown from 1.7 m above the floor with an initial vertical velocity component of 5.1 m s^-1. As it falls into the hoop, its vertical velocity component is 2.1 m s^-1. The rules say the hoop should be d = 3.0 m above the floor. Deduce whether d was 3.0 m.
questions.answer: d = 2.8 m, so the hoop was not at 3.0 m (it was too low).
steps: Vertically: u = 5.1 m s^-1 (up), v = 2.1 m s^-1 (down), a = -9.81 m s^-2.
s = (26.01 - 4.41) / 19.62 = 1.10 m above the release point.
2.8 m is less than 3.0 m, so d was not 3.0 m.

questions.question: A student drops a table tennis ball. It falls for time t and has velocity v just before it hits the ground. The student calculates t and v with the equations of motion, which ignore air resistance. How do the actual values compare with the calculated ones? A: t less, v less; B: t less, v greater; C: t greater, v less; D: t greater, v greater.
questions.answer: C - t greater than calculated, v less than calculated
steps: Air resistance acts upwards on the falling ball, against its motion.
The resultant force is smaller than its weight, so the acceleration is less than 9.81 m s^-2.
With a smaller acceleration the ball takes longer to fall the same height: actual t is greater.
It also gains less speed: actual v is less, so the answer is C.

questions.question: Car A moves at a constant 93 m s^-1 and is 9 m ahead of car B. At this instant car B also moves at 93 m s^-1 but accelerates at a constant 14 m s^-2. Show that the cars are side by side after about 1.1 s.
steps: Measure positions from car B's starting point.
Side by side when s_A = s_B: 9 + 93t = 93t + 7t^2.
t = 1.13 s, about 1.1 s.

questions.question: At the instant shown, car A (constant 93 m s^-1) is 100 m from the finish line and 9 m ahead of car B (93 m s^-1, accelerating at 14 m s^-2). Deduce whether car A reaches the finish line before car B.
questions.answer: Yes - car A finishes first (at 1.08 s B has covered only 108.1 m of the 109 m it needs).
steps: Car A: t = 100 / 93 = 1.075 s to reach the finish line.
Car B must travel 9 + 100 = 109 m to the finish line.
108.1 m is less than 109 m, so car B has not yet reached the line.
Car A reaches the finish line first (consistent with the cars only drawing level at 1.13 s).
